notable_absence.finding: This page's Role-Based Access Control section defines the abstract chain (privileges have a fixed association with roles, which are assigned to users) but, exactly like round 12's finding on the abstract RBAC model elsewhere in the corpus, never names a concrete privilege - only the three role names. See the registry's own hasPrivilege writeup ('PROMOTED FOR WHAT IT DOES NOT CONTAIN').

cross_component_finding: RESOLVES A PRIOR ROUND'S OPEN QUESTION. Round 20's xdcr-filtering-reference-intro.json flagged 'Cluster Administrator' and 'XDCR Administrator' as named-but-unresolved against the registry ('only Full Administrator resolves to an existing registry role'). This round's server/8.0/learn/security/roles.json batch (extracted concurrently) minted role:cluster-admin (now promoted) and role:xdcr-admin (extraction-layer) independently - and this page is the THIRD sibling page in the corpus stating the identical Full/Cluster/XDCR Administrator disjunction verbatim (after xdcr-filtering-reference-intro.md and create-xdcr-reference.md, this same batch), meaning the same access-control fact was written near-identically on three separate pages across two extraction rounds before any single record could resolve all three role names at once.
